description: Poverty and unemployment are major macroeconomic challenges in India. Over time, the government has constituted various expert committees and utilized distinct statistical methods to define the poverty line and measure unemployment accurately.

sections.title: Concept of Poverty and Inequality Measurement
sections.description: The fundamental types of poverty and the scientific methodologies used to measure income and wealth inequality.

key_concepts.explanation: A condition where a person is unable to meet basic human needs such as food, shelter, and clothing. It is measured using a defined threshold known as the 'Poverty Line'.

A measure of income inequality that describes poverty in relation to the economic status of other members of the society. It reflects how much poorer a segment of the population is compared to others.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: A statistical measure of income distribution inequality, ranging from 0 (Perfect Equality) to 1 (Perfect Inequality).
scientific_principles.application: Widely used by economists to gauge the level of wealth or income inequality within a nation or social group.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: A graphical representation of the distribution of income or wealth within a population.
scientific_principles.application: The Gini Coefficient is calculated based on the area between the Lorenz Curve and the hypothetical line of perfect equality.

sections.title: Early Poverty Estimation Committees
sections.description: Pre-independence and early post-independence efforts to measure poverty and establish a poverty line in India.

historical_events.significance: It was the first to define the poverty line based on nutritional requirements, recommending 2400 calories per day for rural areas and 2100 calories per day for urban areas.
Retained the calorie consumption basis but recommended state-specific poverty lines using CPI-AL (Agricultural Labourers) for rural areas and CPI-IW (Industrial Workers) for urban areas.

key_associations.item: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
key_associations.extra_info: He made the earliest estimation of the poverty line in India (1867-68) based on the 'Jail Cost of Living' (estimating Rs. 16 to 35 per capita per year).

sections.title: Modern Poverty Estimation Committees
sections.description: Committees that shifted the paradigm of poverty estimation from purely calorie-based models to comprehensive consumption expenditure.

historical_events.significance: Moved away from the strict calorie-based model to a broader Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE) that included expenditure on health, education, and transport.
Reviewed the Tendulkar methodology and reverted to incorporating distinct calorie, protein, and fat requirements, suggesting separate consumption baskets for rural and urban areas.

important_facts.fact: According to the Tendulkar Committee, the national poverty line was set at Rs. 27 per day for rural areas and Rs. 33 per day for urban areas (for 2011-12).
The Rangarajan Committee revised these thresholds upwards to Rs. 32 per day for rural areas and Rs. 47 per day for urban areas.
Currently, NITI Aayog releases the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) to capture overlapping deprivations in health, education, and living standards.

sections.title: Major Types of Unemployment
sections.description: Different structural and cyclical variations of unemployment observed in an economy.

key_concepts.explanation: A situation where more people are engaged in a job than actually required. The marginal productivity of the extra workers is zero. It is most prevalent in the Indian agriculture sector.
Occurs due to a mismatch between the skills possessed by the workers and the requirements of the available jobs, usually driven by technological changes or shifts in the economy's structure.
A temporary form of unemployment that happens when individuals are in transition between jobs or are searching for a new job. Also known as 'Search Unemployment'.
Unemployment resulting from the fluctuations in the business cycle, specifically caused by a deficiency in aggregate demand during economic recessions or downturns.

important_facts.fact: Educated Unemployment, where individuals with formal degrees are unable to find suitable jobs, is a prominent and growing problem primarily in the urban areas of India.

sections.title: Measurement of Unemployment in India
sections.description: The standard approaches utilized by the National Statistical Office (NSO) to measure employment and unemployment rates.

key_concepts.explanation: A long-term approach that measures employment over a reference period of 365 days. A person is considered unemployed if they had no work for the major part of the year despite being available.
A short-term measure where a person is considered unemployed if they did not find even one hour of gainful work on any day during the reference week (preceding 7 days).
The most comprehensive measure that records the activity status of an individual for each day of the reference week in terms of person-days, effectively capturing underemployment.

key_associations.extra_info: Launched in 2017, this survey provides regular and frequent data on the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), and Unemployment Rate in India.
